non_blocking: Accept-case EREs in tools/similar_guard_controls.sh pin the floor value literally (SIMILAR_MINOR \(14\)) in the pristine/future/comment cases. If the protocol ever raises SIMILAR_MINOR above 14, the controls go red at the pristine case even though the guard is correct; a one-line ERE update would be needed. Low risk (SIMILAR_MINOR is a feature marker, not a version), and it fails loudly rather than silently.

The S0.3 check greps the whole of main.gd for the literal 'SIMILAR_MINOR', so a future code COMMENT mentioning 'SIMILAR_MINOR' (e.g. documenting the floor) would fail the guard with the misleading message 'main.gd asks SIMILAR_MINOR'. Fail-closed, but the message does not distinguish a name from a mention in a comment.

Scope is by design the map session only: the guard constrains _run_map, while other sessions legitimately request lower minors (main.gd:414 _run_interior asks SimBridge.ISM_MINOR (8); _run_transit sets 2). The guard therefore proves 'the map session asks >= 14', not 'the game always asks >= 14'. The design states this scope explicitly; noting it so a future reader does not over-read the guarantee.

The broad 'want_minor' occurrence count (revision 2) also counts substrings, so a future identifier such as want_minor_x would over-count and fail closed with 'mentions want_minor N times'. Fail-closed by design; only a nuisance if the name changes.

mutants.description: (a1) Scratch copy of main.gd + bridge/sim_bridge.gd; _run_map's requested minor downgraded below 14 in a realistic GDScript form that still names SimBridge constants: 'sim.want_minor=min(SimBridge.EARTH_LOG_MINOR,SimBridge.SURFACE_MINOR)' (effectively 13). Guard run as 'make -s similar-main-guard SIMILAR_GUARD_ROOT=<scratch>'. Guard replied 'main.gd _run_map want_minor is not one bare SimBridge minor' (the call is not one bare constant) and make exited 2.

(a2) Scratch copy; realistic GDScript alias downgrade: a local 'var wanted: int = SimBridge.SURFACE_MINOR' (13) assigned by 'sim.want_minor=wanted'. want_minor is mentioned exactly once (so the count check passes) but the right-hand side is not a bare SimBridge constant; guard replied 'not one bare SimBridge minor', make exited 2.

(a3) Scratch copy; a new below-floor constant 'const LEGACY_MINOR := 13' added to bridge/sim_bridge.gd and asked by _run_map (grammar-valid, resolves cleanly) - a pure floor-logic attack. Guard replied 'main.gd _run_map asks LEGACY_MINOR (13) below SIMILAR_MINOR (14)', make exited 2.

(b1) Scratch root (Makefile, mk/, main.gd, bridge/sim_bridge.gd, tools/similar_guard_controls.sh) with ONE guard check weakened: the floor comparison 'test "$$want" -ge "$$floor"' replaced by 'test 1 = 1'. 'make -s -C <scratch> similar-guard-controls' went red at the 'below' case ('below: make rc 0, want 2', with the guard's ok line 'asks SURFACE_MINOR (13) >= SIMILAR_MINOR (14)'), the script exited 1 and make exited 2.

(b2) Scratch root with a DIFFERENT single check weakened: the S0.3 line 'if grep -q SIMILAR_MINOR "$$g"; then' replaced by 'if false; then'. The controls went red at the 'exact' case ('exact: make rc 0, want 2', ok line 'asks SIMILAR_MINOR (14) >= SIMILAR_MINOR (14)'), script exit 1, make exit 2.

ASSESSMENT. The implementation matches the approved design's Appendix A/B byte-for-byte, the guard fails closed on every mutation tried (grammar, count, floor, resolution, S0.3), the committed controls prove the guard still guards (13 rejections / 3 acceptances, including the computed future-protocol-bump cases), and the wiring puts both targets in similar-test and ci-fast. The five independent mutants I wrote (including two the committed controls do not contain: a min() call downgrade and a local-alias downgrade) were all killed with rc=2, and two one-check weakenings of the guard recipe were both caught by the controls at the expected case. No blocking finding. Score 95: full credit on the behaviour and scope, minus a small amount for the four non-blocking brittleness/clarity observations above (hard-coded floor 14 in the accept EREs, whole-file SIMILAR_MINOR grep vs comments, the deliberately narrow _run_map scope, and substring counting of want_minor) - none of which changes the guard's fail-closed behaviour. Not committed, per the brief.
